question: When the Bank of Canada says it has changed its policy interest rate, which rate is it talking about?
generated_answer:
The Bank of Canada can directly influence a short-term interest rate called the target for the overnight rate. You may have heard it being referred to as the policy interest rate, the key interest rate or the overnight rate. 2. How does the Bank of Canada make a decision on interest rates? The Bank makes monetary policy decisions eight times a year. Before each decision, we analyze a lot of economic data to get a sense of how the economy is doing. We think about how we can achieve our target for keeping inflation low and stable. We consider the current state of the economy, the state of the labour market and the outlook for the global economy. We also consider a lot of other indicators. We look at the effects of everything that’s happening both here in Canada and around the world. 3. What is the role of the target for the overnight rate? We use the target for the overnight rate to try to influence how much it costs to borrow. Interest rates affect the economy in a couple of ways:

They influence how much people borrow. For example, when interest rates go up, it costs more to borrow. This means that people borrow less. They influence how much people spend. For example, when interest rates go up, some people spend less because the goods they want to buy have become more expensive. 4. How do changes in the overnight rate affect other interest rates? When we change our target for the overnight rate, it sends a signal to the market that influences how much people have to pay to borrow money. Lenders then adjust the interest rates they charge their borrowers. Banks and other lenders base their interest rates on market rates. Take the prime rate for example. It’s the rate banks reserve for their best customers. Lenders will offer lower interest rates to borrowers if they consider them to be a lower risk of defaulting on their loans. So, if you have a good credit score, lenders are more likely to offer you a lower interest rate than someone with a poor credit score. 5. How do interest rates affect the economy? When we raise the overnight rate, we encourage people to save money and pay down debt. As people borrow less, they spend less. This reduces pressure on prices to go up. When we lower the overnight rate, we encourage people to borrow and spend. As a result, economic growth is likely to accelerate. But this also tends to lead to higher inflation—prices go up more quickly. 6. What is the best interest rate for a strong economy? There isn’t one. That’s because the economy changes over time. Interest rates have to adjust to the economic conditions. For example, when the economy is facing a rapid increase in inflation, it means that people are spending a lot of money. Higher interest rates help slow the economy down and curb inflation. When the economy is facing a slowdown or recession, higher interest rates will make things worse. In this case, lower interest rates can boost the economy by encouraging people to spend and borrow more. 7. How does the exchange rate affect the economy? The exchange rate also plays an important role in the Canadian economy. It can influence, for example, the prices we pay for imports and how competitive Canadian exporters are in world markets. The exchange rate can also affect the prices of goods and services in our economy. For example, if the value of the Canadian dollar goes down, imports from the United States will cost more. This can put upward pressure on the prices of those goods in Canadian dollar terms. 8. How do we measure inflation? We measure inflation by the movement in the consumer price index (CPI), which is the average price of a set of goods and services that Canadians typically buy. The rate of inflation is the percentage change in the price level from one period to another—for example, from one year to the next. 9. What is core inflation? The prices of some items, such as fruits and vegetables, tend to respond to changes in economic conditions in the short term. To find out what is happening to prices in general, we look at the CPI for a basket of goods and services that is representative of what Canadians buy, but excludes some of the most volatile components of the CPI. This is called core inflation. 10. What is a flexible exchange rate? A flexible exchange rate system means that the value of the currency rises and falls on the foreign exchange rate market, depending on the supply of, and demand for, that currency. Some countries, like the United States and China, have a fixed exchange rate. In a fixed exchange rate system, the central bank intervenes in the foreign exchange market by buying and selling its own currency to try to keep its value constant against another currency. 11.
